definition: each part as one solid: the closed surface that holds its residues' own volume (0.135 nm³ for each amino acid, 0.32 nm³ for each nucleotide), protein and nucleic acid together, in a cloud where each residue is spread as a Gaussian 1.8 nm wide weighted by its volume, on a grid 1.8 nm apart (coarser than the setting's 1.6 nm, to hold the budget); of a surface in pieces, its largest and every piece of at least 5% of its volume are kept, smaller ones dropped (listed under dropped); for two tones, that solid divided where the nucleic acid's share of the cloud is the greater and where the protein's is (under tones, each inside the solid or on it)
illustration: The viewer's own surface of the entry's coordinates, an illustration: not the structure, and nothing of the entry is copied but the numbers worked out here. The Protein Data Bank states no surface.
title: Structure of human mitochondrial COX1-translating ribosome nascent chain complex with tRNAs in initial hybrid state (H1)
frame: the measuring tool's frame: origin at the centre of the whole's atoms; y from the part large's centre to the part small's; x the whole's longest axis made square to y; z = x × y
